renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: gap_length_matrix
  title: Gap length distribution per assembly
  description: |-
    Each row is an assembly and each column a bin of gap length on a log10 scale, coloured by the share of that assembly's runs of N that fall in the bin. It answers how an assembly was scaffolded and whether two assemblies used the same gap sizes.
    How to read: a single dark cell means one fixed gap length, typical of a filler inserted by a scaffolder. A spread across many bins means estimated gap sizes. The curve on top is the mean over the assemblies shown.
    Note: seqtk cutN reports runs of N, which stand for assembly gaps. Rows are compared as shares, so assemblies with few and with many gaps share one scale.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lh3/seqtk/master/seqtk.c
  kind: signal_matrix
  config:
    reference_position: -1
  roles:
    region_id: genome
    position: log10_gap_length
    value: gaps_pct

- component: advanced_viz
  id: gap_length_profile
  title: Gaps per length bin
  description: |-
    Each curve is an assembly: the number of its gaps in each length bin, on a log scale of gap length. It answers which gap sizes dominate each assembly.
    How to read: a sharp peak is a fixed gap length. A broad curve means gap sizes were estimated. Compare the heights with care, because an assembly with many gaps dwarfs one with few, and the matrix tile puts them on one scale.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lh3/seqtk/master/seqtk.c
  kind: profile
  config:
    log_x: true
    x_title: Gap length (bp)
    y_title: Gaps per bin
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: genome
    x: gap_length_bp
    y: gaps

- component: figure
  title: Assembly gaps per log10 length bin
  description: |-
    Each line is an assembly: the number of gaps in each bin of log10 gap length. It answers the same question as the profile tile, in a plain figure that can be exported.
    How to read: peaks show the dominant gap sizes of an assembly, and lines that peak at the same place were scaffolded in the same way.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lh3/seqtk/master/seqtk.c
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: log10_gap_length
    y: gaps
    color: genome
    labels:
      log10_gap_length: Gap length (log10 bp)
      gaps: Gaps per bin
      genome: Assembly

- component: table
  title: Gap length bins
  description: |-
    Each row is an assembly and a bin of gap length, with the number of gaps, their share of the assembly's gaps and the bases they cover. It answers the exact counts behind the matrix.
    How to read: filter by assembly and sort by gap length to see its gap sizes in order.

- component: figure
  title: Bases in assembly gaps per genome
  description: |-
    Each bar is an assembly, with the total bases that sit in runs of N, on a log scale. It answers which assemblies carry the most unresolved sequence.
    How to read: a tall bar is a gap-rich assembly, which covers less of a target without being more divergent. Compare it with the number of gaps in the table to tell a few long gaps from many short ones.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median number of bases in gaps of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Seqtk.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lh3/seqtk/master/seqtk.c
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: genome
    y: gap_bp
    log_y: true
    labels:
      genome: Assembly
      gap_bp: Bases in gaps
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: gap_bp

- component: card
  id: gap_runs
  title: Gaps per assembly
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of runs of N per assembly, with the smallest and largest count. It answers how gapped the assemblies are.
    How to read: a count near zero means a gap-free assembly. Thousands of gaps mean a scaffolded draft, whose gaps cannot align to a target.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lh3/seqtk/master/seqtk.c
  column: gaps
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: grid
  caption: median, with the fewest and the most

- component: card
  id: gap_bases
  title: Bases in gaps
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of bases inside runs of N over the assemblies in view, with the median and the largest per assembly. It answers how much sequence is unresolved.
    How to read: a large maximum against a small median points to one assembly that is far more gapped than the rest. Open the gap table to find it.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lh3/seqtk/master/seqtk.c
  column: gap_bp
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: grid
  caption: total, with the median and largest assembly
  headline: true

- component: interactive
  title: Gap count range
  description: Filters the tiles to assemblies whose number of gaps falls inside the chosen range.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: gaps

- component: table
  title: Assembly gaps table
  description: |-
    Each row is an assembly with its number of gaps, their total and median length, the longest gap and how many sequences carry one. It answers the exact numbers behind every tile and lets a row selection filter the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by total gap bases to rank the assemblies by unresolved sequence.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: genome
